catalyst_rule: Option 3: drop it entirely. Drafts and blessings can supply a Catalyst.

batch1.what_keeps_stages_earned: No limit, just money: Stages can simply be bought, and the wealthy are stronger because they're wealthy. Class warfare sits at the center of the world, with lucky commoners holding monster cores as the great threat to it.
how_you_get_a_wellspring: At a Core, in a dungeon
batch1.typology_doubling: Grows with mastery: it starts as a small boost and reaches double only for someone who has lived with that lens for years, like a Trait growing.
batch1.who_can_use_fate: Rare, mostly bloodline: Hataraki and a few other bloodlines hold real Fate Arts, some high-Stage masters reach it late, the Fate Path stays very hard, and most people only touch Fate through a blessing or a Master Work Draft.

batch2.trait_growth: Trait levels: each Trait has its own number that goes up with use, like a skill in a LitRPG.
batch2.skills: Yes, skills level with use: every practitioner has skills that rise by doing them and show as Grades on the sheet; techniques are named things done with them.
batch2.the_sheet: Full system windows: level-up notices and sheets on the page in blocks, LitRPG style, even mid-fight.

batch3.what_a_window_is: The Crystal reading itself: the Soul Crystal is the soul and the Continuum measures it, so the window is the soul reporting its numbers to its owner in their own tongue; no one else can see it; scholars argue about who built it.
batch3.windows_on_the_page: Often and detailed: regular windows for damage, skill gains and reserve, mid-fight, like a true LitRPG.
batch3.experience: Yes, by danger overcome: killing something stronger moves Level more than a hundred weak kills; crews argue over who got the kill.
batch3.old_scenes: New scenes only: archived scenes stay as written; new writing uses windows; NATALIE and the prose rules get updated.

batch4.raw_cores: Yes, and it's deadly: a core can be swallowed or broken raw, taking everything at once with no alchemist's fee; most die or come out wrong.
batch4.monsters: Yes, they eat and evolve: monsters gain Levels by killing, each other included, and change form at their own thresholds; a famous monster has a name and a bounty, its window readable by strong enough Gnosis.
batch4.dungeons: Floors and a heart: a dungeon grows down in levels around its Core, more dangerous as you go, with something at the bottom guarding the heart; kill that and clear it, or leave it and it grows.
batch4.classes: Paths are the classes: Body, Spirit, Attraction and Fate are what people mean by class, shown on the window and sheet, with crews built around them and slang by culture. SUPERSEDED by his later word: 'aether class are supposed to be classed like in unbound'. Details open.

batch5.window_numbers: Grades and bars, no raw EU: windows show Grades, percentages and levels; EU, AU/s and eta stay in the notes.
batch5.technique_rank: Names only: techniques do not show levels, only the bigger name when they jump; Traits and skills carry the numbers.
batch5.blessings_on_sheet: Listed, sometimes lying: a blessing shows as its own line, and one that is really a curse may read as a gift for years because the giver wrote the line.

batch6.bought_release: Release must be learned: a bought Stage opens the door, but you still find and master your own Release by fighting; a rich Stage IX may have none while a poor fighter at the same Stage has all three.
batch6.domains: Everyone who reaches it, each unique: anyone at Stage VIII can have one, their own concept made real; fame, rivalries and bounties follow.
batch6.release_in_window: Big and loud: calling a Release fills the window with its name and what changed, and a timer bar starts draining.
batch6.boost_cap: Keep two Grades: only outside help goes past it, and blessings could count as outside help.

batch7.crafts: Crafts are skills anyone can level: any practitioner can learn any craft and it rises with use; a guild's title is how far they have gone.
batch7.master_works: Beyond what the rules allow: a piece that does something its Grade and material should not be able to do, made once at the end of a lifetime, always Unique or Mythic, and named.
batch7.monster_gear: Yes, and bonded gear grows: scale, bone and hide make top gear; a bonded weapon grows with its owner and its window line changes; everyone else's gear stays what it is.
batch7.appraising: Assay and a trade skill: an Appraisal skill and an assay instrument read an item, strong Gnosis helps, and a good forger can beat a weak appraiser.
batch7.crafts_later_word: Isaac, same night: remove the different crafts; they are not needed.

batch8.sheet_size: Primaries, Sub-Stats when they matter: a normal look shows the Eight Primaries with Grades; a Sub-Stat appears when used or when it moves; the full sixty-four stay available to study.
batch8.stat_points: Your life spends most, you steer some: what you do raises those stats, and a few points are yours to place at each Stage.
batch8.monster_sheets: Same scale, readable by Gnosis: a monster has a Level, Grades and Threat Tier on the same ladder; a weak Gnosis gets question marks.
batch8.reading_people: Gnosis against Ward, can be hidden: a stronger Gnosis Perception reads a weaker Resilience Ward, everything else is an estimate said aloud, and people can hide or fake it.

batch9.aether_class: Named classes on the old ladder: at thresholds the soul is offered a class that fits how the person has lived; it gives abilities and shapes growth; the old ladder stays as its tier.
batch9.aura_look: Family color, Wellspring texture: Family sets the base color, a Wellspring adds texture and sound, a class or big Trait adds a shape.
batch9.pressure: Felt first, window second: the room reacts first as on file, then the window reports a debuff line; a Grandmaster merchant with no fighting Stage has no Pressure at all.

batch10.the_dead: Yes, and it's the great crime: a dead practitioner's Crystal can be taken and rendered into the strongest Drafts of all; it is the worst crime in every realm and the most profitable, and it is behind the unexplained surplus of Crystal Draw.
batch10.epochs: Rarely, and it shakes the world: Epochs and Archons act seldom; lesser spirits and high-Stage people give most of the world's blessings.
batch10.races: Race on the window, real differences: race and lineage show on the sheet and shape base stats and what comes easily; classes and suitable Wellsprings differ.
batch10.sects: What money can't buy: sects teach Releases, Domains, techniques, skills and the rites for their Wellspring, and bring real fights, crews and a name.

batch11.law_timing: Now, and adjust as we go: index as R84, update Natalie and the pipelines, and the next scene uses windows.
batch11.windows_in_rp: Same blocks, you control your PC's: windows appear in turns and Discord posts as plain text blocks; his PC's gains are offered as window lines he keeps or changes.
batch11.cards: Convert with the R82 rollout: each card gets concept, moves, class, Trait levels and skills in one pass; other creators' cards stay untouched; starts with the pilot three.

batch12.curses: Same power, wrong terms: a curse is often a blessing with terms you did not read or a giver who does not care what you want; nobody can tell at first, and some are both.
batch12.class_trees: Evolves by how you live it: a class grows at each tier into a form chosen from what you have done, some shared by many and some held by one person; a class gives skills and shapes moves, and the one wild concept stays the person's own.
batch12.monster_ranks: Threat Tier, then a name: monsters are graded T1 to T9 like commissions; a famous one earns a name, an epithet and a bounty.
batch12.dungeons_fight_back: Alive and learning: a dungeon adapts around its Core, moves galleries, breeds what kills crews best and pays attention to who keeps coming back; each has a personality by its Wellspring; scholars argue whether it thinks.
